I like this game a lot. When I heard that they were closing up shop, I decided to give this game another try. 
I bought this one along with the first Doom & Destiny about 4 years ago, but for some reason never played it. It felt a little weird not having a save function but it autosaves. I had a great time getting into the battle system. I ended up playing 10 hours straight. I didn't want to put it down. 
But when I did, I found out the game has a problem with One Drive or Windows 11 because when I tried to play it again, it wouldn't run. It just froze at the title screen. One Drive popped up a notice asking if it was okay to delete some 2200 files. I declined and waited for the game to load. It never did nor could I get it to run at all. So I deleted those files from One Drive and tried to reinstall it and try again. It worked just fine and I played for a bit. I made sure the save icon appeared in the upper left corner of the screen. I shut it down and tried to run the game again. Same thing. The game wouldn't run, One Drive, again, asked if I wanted to delete over 2000 files. This time I agreed, but the same thing happened.
So, I can play the game but only if I keep it running until I finish the game. Then I read through the reviews and found that I'm not the only one with this problem.
If you decide to purchase this game, make sure you can shut it down and restart it before your two hour limit is reached.

Doom & Destiny Advanced is a fantastic RPG that combines humor, classic turn-based combat, and a great narrative into one package. The game is packed with witty dialogue and hilarious references to nerd culture, making every scene a joy to experience. The combat system is surprisingly deep, with plenty of customization options that let you build your party how you want. You’ll be exploring a vast world filled with secret locations, epic battles, and lots of side quests. The mix of humor and gameplay keeps things fresh, and the constant nods to classic RPG tropes make it feel like a love letter to the genre. 

One standout aspect is the sheer variety of enemies and abilities. You’ll constantly be unlocking new strategies and powers as you progress, which keeps combat engaging. The game’s difficulty curve is also well-tuned, offering enough challenge to keep you on your toes without ever feeling overwhelming. The pixel art is charming, and the soundtrack fits perfectly, enhancing the overall experience.

Whether you’re a longtime RPG fan or someone looking for a hilarious and well-designed game, Doom & Destiny Advanced has a little something for everyone. It’s one of those games where the more you put in, the more you get out, with tons of secrets and post-game content that makes it worth playing long after the main story ends.

I remember playing Doom & Destiny when I was younger, now here I am playing D&D Advanced, so far enjoying it!

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Played Doom and Destiny before playing this game. Was a bit disappointed with the story overall. Felt a bit generic, and far less tongue in cheek compared to their first game. This one felt like they were taking themselves far more seriously, while simultaneously trying to be funny with some toilet humor, as well as many cultural references. However I did enjoy the additional job classes that this game offered. Some of the classes felt far more powerful than others, while other job classes felt mostly useless. There were some quality of life changes from the first game that I liked, while some of the changes that they made from the first game seemed like a step back. But overall, the length of the game felt perfect for an indie game. I would definitely recommend playing the game, as I put nearly 300 hours into it and plan on playing it again in the future.
